<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{
  "body_md": "## Problem
Staff are forced to retrain repeatedly when interface elements move without warning, causing errors and delays in claims and payments processing. This disrupts workflow and wastes time because changes are released without preview or notice.

## Who is affected
- **Claims and payments processing teams** across multiple accounts, who must retrain staff when controls shift unexpectedly, leading to errors and operational disruption [i:27a70a943d3863cd] [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f] [i:71a03e5a571c2a63].
- **Account managers and support teams** who field complaints about the disruption and the need for more predictable release processes [i:1510a29a4fb29690] [i:1b3b992fef61581a] [i:ad38c9f354762a62].
- **Onboarding teams** who are asked by clients for ways to preview changes before they go live [i:1b469b41c095b4da].

## Evidence
- The issue has been raised 21 times across 7 accounts via 4 different routes: support (7 mentions), sales (6 mentions), account management (6 mentions), and onboarding (2 mentions) [i:044bdc94d943b6b0] [i:1510a29a4fb29690] [i:211006eeabec013f].
- Specific, high-value accounts have reported the problem. Wexmoor Motor (ARR £1,950,000) stated that an update moved the ‘reserves’ button, forcing them to retrain half the team [i:044bdc94d943b6b0]. Linnet House Insurance (ARR £360,000) reported that a vanished Claims Tasks panel required mid-week retraining [i:9c432aa4bd712320]. Quillon Business Insurance (ARR £860,000) said unexpected changes keep shifting controls, causing staff errors [i:27a70a943d3863cd].
- The financial impact is significant, with the total ARR of the citing accounts being £7,360,000 [i:a590adfec9690173] [i:bd1bd40a6ba477f6]. The problem is linked to tangible business costs, as one customer noted it is disruptive and costly [i:4178fecee898fafd].
- Customers explicitly request advance notice, previews, and bundled releases to mitigate the disruption [i:1510a29a4fb29690] [i:1b3b992fef61581a] [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f]. They need predictability so staff can focus on policyholders, not relearning the software [i:d3cbea3941929ea5] [i:7dccff3918b6f081].

## Why now
- Customer feedback has been consistent and recent, with mentions spanning from September to October 2026 [i:a590adfec9690173] [i:fc1d63199de541cf].
- The issue directly impacts customer retention risk. In the last 90 days, only 1 renewal has occurred, while several major accounts have upcoming renewal dates, including Stannary Commercial on 2026-12-05 and Hollinbrook Home Insurance on 2027-01-15 [i:3a4ae29f32b5253f] [i:a590adfec9690173].
- The problem is pervasive across the customer base, affecting accounts of all sizes and through every customer-facing route, indicating it is a systemic pain point requiring immediate attention to protect revenue and customer satisfaction.",
  "citations": ["044bdc94d943b6b0", "27a70a943d3863cd", "3a4ae29f32b5253f", "71a03e5a571c2a63", "1510a29a4fb29690", "1b3b992fef61581a", "ad38c9f354762a62", "1b469b41c095b4da", "211006eeabec013f", "9c432aa4bd712320", "a590adfec9690173", "bd1bd40a6ba477f6", "4178fecee898fafd", "d3cbea3941929ea5", "7dccff3918b6f081", "fc1d63199de541cf"]
}
